title: QASparse: Query-Adaptive Sparse Attention with Tailored Budgets and Tokens
abstract: arXiv:2611.29280v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Long-sequence inference in large language models is constrained by the high cost of prefilling, where dense attention scales quadratically with context length. Exploiting similarity across attention heads offers a way to reduce redundant computation. Prior approaches in this direction have relied on localized query observations to determine head-level computation reuse or budget allocation. However, inter-head similarity does not imply uniform query requirements, leaving adaptation to varying budget needs and selection preferences across query regions a key challenge. We introduce QASparse, a Query-Adaptive Sparse attention mechanism with hardware-efficient execution. QASparse preserves the efficiency of shared cross-head importance estimation while adapting computational budgets and token selections to query requirements, and it executes these dynamic sparse decisions through dedicated kernels. translated_abstract: 大型语言模型中的长序列推理受到预填充阶段高成本的制约，其中密集注意力的计算量随上下文长度呈二次方增长。利用注意力头之间的相似性提供了一种减少冗余计算的途径。此前这一方向的方法依赖于局部的查询观测来确定头级别的计算复用或预算分配。然而，头间相似性并不意味着各查询区域具有统一的需求，因此如何适应不同查询区域变化的预算需求和令牌选择偏好成为一个关键挑战。我们提出了QASparse，一种具备硬件高效执行能力的查询自适应稀疏注意力机制。QASparse在保留共享跨头重要性估计效率的同时，使计算预算和令牌选择适应查询需求，并通过专用内核执行这些动态稀疏决策。其查询自适应性源于两个（内容在此处截断）……
tldr: QASparse提出了一种查询自适应的稀疏注意力机制，在保留跨头共享重要性估计效率的同时，根据查询需求动态定制计算预算与令牌选择，并借助专用内核高效执行，从而加速大模型长序列预填充推理。
en_tdlr: QASparse is a query-adaptive sparse attention mechanism that preserves the efficiency of shared cross-head importance estimation while dynamically tailoring computational budgets and token selections to query requirements through dedicated kernels, accelerating long-sequence prefilling in large language models.
